Energy Improvements in Rural or Remote Areas Background Rural communities face a unique set of energy challenges due to their smaller populations and isolation from larger electrical systems, including higher electric bills, unreliable energy supplies, and/or no access to electricity at all. Nearly 50 million Americans live in rural or remote areas where energy costs are often disproportionately high and service can be unreliable. At the same time, America has vast unused potential for new energy resources with nearly 97% of the country’s land mass considered rural. Program Overview The Energy Improvements in Rural or Remote Areas (ERA) program gives communities with 10,000 or fewer people the tools and resources they need to improve the resilience, reliability, and affordability of their local energy systems. These community-driven projects enable residents to make the right decisions about their own energy, economic, cultural, and geographic needs. Developing technology to store electrical energy so it can be available to meet demand whenever needed would represent a major breakthrough in electricity distribution. Helping to try and meet this goal, electricity storage devices can manage the amount of power required to supply customers at times when need is greatest, which is during peak load. These devices can also help make renewable energy, whose power output cannot be controlled by grid operators, smooth and dispatchable. They can also balance microgrids to achieve a good match between generation and load. Storage devices can provide frequency regulation to maintain the balance between the network's load and power generated, and they can achieve a more reliable power supply for high tech industrial facilities. Seeking to understand and transform the world’s energy systems, MIT researchers and students investigate all aspects of energy. They discover new ways of generating and storing energy, as in creating biofuels from plant waste and in holding electricity from renewable sources in cost-effective, high-capacity batteries. They create models and design experiments to determine how we can improve energy efficiency at all scales, from nanostructures and photovoltaic cells to large power plants and smart electrical grids. They analyze how people make decisions about energy, whether as individual consumers or whole nations, and they forecast what the social and environmental consequences of these decisions might be. In fact, the study of energy is so important and so pervasive at MIT, the MIT Energy Initiative has devised an undergraduate Energy Studies Minor which develops the expertise needed to reshape how the world uses energy. Unlike static materials, biological systems and processes can be difficult to measure because they are always changing. NIST develops solutions for these measurement problems to help the U.S. maintain leadership of the global bioeconomy . Engineering biology, also known as synthetic biology, enables the intentional design, manufacture and deployment of living cells, cell systems, and other biological processes to create materials and products that benefit us, like crops that resist drought and pests, renewable energy sources, advanced medicines, and more. "Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. Jones sat stony-faced in the coaching box as the message appeared again in the midst of his team's 78-15 thrashing at England's hands on Saturday. There was little for him to enjoy on his return to Twickenham, where he was head coach for seven years. But, for the rest of a capacity crowd, it was a fun one. Attribution England Men 0:24 Nick Mashiter Football reporter Image source, Getty Images Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon has vowed to be more selfish ahead of facing Aston Villa. The England forward is preparing for the Champions League clash on Tuesday following his summer move from Newcastle in a deal worth more than £69m. Gordon has helped Barca to the top of La Liga and has scored three goals in 13 appearances in all competitions, including one in Saturday's 6-1 win over Alaves. But the 25-year-old wants to do more to help Hansi Flick's side complete a clean sweep of trophies this season. "The challenge of joining Barca is different to what I've had before because I was fighting relegation for two or three years (at Everton), which was tough," he said. "At Newcastle we were fighting for the Champions League and to push up the table and now fighting for Barca for every trophy. "To be competing on every front for every trophy is definitely the most enjoyable. I think people think it's more pressure but it's actually less pressure than fighting relegation and fighting to push up the table for the Champions League. "I want to win every trophy. pages.description: England manager Thomas Tuchel omits Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face Spain on Sunday night.
pages.text: England team news: Thomas Tuchel omits Jarrad Branthwaite, James Garner and Josh King for Spain game - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, James Garner played as a substitute against Croatia on Thursday, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Josh King were unused By Sami Mokbel Senior football correspondent Published 15 November 2026 England manager Thomas Tuchel has omitted Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday night. England travelled to Spain with a squad of 26 players but Uefa rules state that only 23 players can be selected in a matchday squad for Nations League games The return to fitness of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence - who missed Thursday's win over Croatia - has been a contributing factor in the trio's omission. Arsenal defender Konsa could come straight back into the starting XI while James Trafford will replace Jordan Pickford in goal. Garner replaced Declan Rice in the 77th minute of the 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley, scoring a goal that was subsequently disallowed, while Everton team-mate Branthwaite and Fulham's King were unused substitutes. King received his first senior call-up for the two final Nations League fixtures in Group A3, but the midfielder, 19, will not feature in this international window. However, fellow first-time call-ups Jobe Bellingham and James Hill are included. The Bath man burst on to the international scene in a man-of-the-match display against Argentina at the end of 2025, but has not played for his country in the 12 months since. Ojomoh was initially left out of Steve Borthwick's wider training squad but after starring for the 'A' team has been catapulted back into the England number 12 shirt and with it World Cup contention. "Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby," boss Steve Borthwick told BBC Sport. "His ability to see space and distribute, to hide where he is going to pass and to pass short or long, that's a rare skill." pages.text: England v New Zealand: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie says team 'let the country down' in Wales defeat - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 16 November 2026 New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie has demanded a reaction against England on Saturday after saying the All Blacks "let the country down" in their historic defeat by Wales. In one of the great upsets of the professional era, New Zealand lost 35-28 in Cardiff at the weekend, a first defeat against the Welsh in 73 years. New Zealand will face an in-form England in Twickenham as they look to avoid back-to-back Nations Championship losses, with Rennie vowing not to brush the Wales result "under the carpet". "It's important we poke each other in the chest at the start of the week," Rennie said. "You have to front up and take things on the chin, all of us. Come Saturday, our mindset will be fully on England and our job is to perform. "We will be highly motivated for the weekend, but we won't brush the [Wales] result under the carpet. "[The players] are feeling it. They know we let ourselves down and we let the country down." A close-up of his own face on the Twickenham big screen. A painful inquest under the sticks. Jack van Poortvliet's first meeting with New Zealand was only four minutes old when it curdled sour. Van Poortvliet was touted as the next big thing at Test level too. But, off an early England line-out, Van Poortvliet, focused on Owen Farrell's hands, failed to spot Dalton Papali'i flying up out of the line. pages.text: England v New Zealand: Seb Atkinson 'ticking off wishes and dreams' as All Blacks loom - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Atkinson has won eight England caps since making his Test debut in July 2025 By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 17 November 2026 England centre Seb Atkinson says he is living a childhood dream as he prepares to face New Zealand in Twickenham on Saturday. The Gloucester pivot has recovered from a hip knock and is set to return to the starting XV at number 12 for the visit of the wounded All Blacks. For Atkinson, this weekend's game comes a fortnight after he made his first Allianz Stadium appearance with England in the 45-22 thumping of Australia. "It's sort of ticking off wishes and dreams that you have as a young aspiring rugby player," Atkinson told BBC Sport. "Watching [England against New Zealand in 2012] when Manu [Tuilagi] scored that try and set up that try, the big performance in the semi-final of the World Cup a few years ago [in 2019]. "And obviously I was frustrated to not be available last year when the team put in a good performance. "So a lot of things spring to mind and to be able to be out there and show what I can do on that stage will be really exciting for me personally." pages.description: Sarina Wiegman says she "cannot think of a better job in football" as she commits to staying on as manager of the Lionesses until after Euro 2029.
pages.text: England women's manager Sarina Wiegman signs two-year contract extension - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has been in charge of England for more than five years By Paul Battison BBC Sport Journalist Published 19 October 2026 England manager Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension with the Lionesses. The 56-year-old's previous deal was due to expire after next summer's World Cup, but her new contract will run until the end of Euro 2029. Dutchwoman Wiegman guided England to their second straight European Championship title with victory over Spain in the Euro 2025 final. The victory meant the Lionesses became the first England team - women's or men's - to win a major trophy on foreign soil. "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," said Wiegman. "Working for a world-class organisation like The FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day." England thrashed Greece 8-1 on aggregate last week to qualify for round two of the World Cup play-offs, where they will face Ukraine. Should the Lionesses win that two-legged tie, they will qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil. "My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added. pages.title: England: Alessia Russo named women's player of the year - BBC Sport
pages.description: Arsenal forward Alessia Russo is named England women's player of the year after scoring five goals in 10 games.
pages.text: England: Alessia Russo named women's player of the year - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Alessia Russo has scored 31 goals in 68 games for England By Paul Battison BBC Sport Journalist Published 11 October 2026 Forward Alessia Russo has been named England women's player of the year. The 27-year-old, who also won the award two seasons ago, has been a key player in the 2025-26 campaign, featuring in all 10 games and scoring five goals. She started nine of those games, including all six of England's 2027 World Cup qualifiers. Last week, she scored the third goal as England beat Greece 3-1 in their 2027 World Cup play-off semi-final first leg, with the second leg at Leicester's King Power Stadium on Tuesday. Arsenal's Russo pipped Chelsea pair Lucy Bronze and Hannah Hampton to the award, which is voted for by fans. "To receive the award is really special, particularly as it comes directly from the fans. I am so grateful for their support," said Russo. Russo is among 30 players who were nominated in September for the women's Ballon d'Or, with Alex Greenwood the only other English player on the shortlist. Figure caption, 'Russo needs to start as a nine for England' "A big thank you also to my team-mates - it is always about the collective," Russo added. Russo has represented England at every stage from under-15s level upwards and won her first senior international cap when she came on as a substitute against Spain in the final game of the 2020 SheBelieves Cup. The tips of Rock’s ears quiver as he fixates on the flock. He has just one thing on his mind: herding his master’s sheep, as generations of working dogs have done before him. His body is tense, but still he waits for the signal. I’m in Yorkshire Dales National Park, watching a demonstration with international sheepdog trialist Richard Fawcett on his farm just outside the town of Hawes, where he’s putting his dogs through their paces. He breathes a barely audible “come-bye” and Rock whips clockwise around the flock in a pear-shaped arc. pages.text: English Standards English Standards Skip Navigation English Standards The U.S. Census Bureau’s Statistics in Schools (SIS) activities are based on relevant education standards and guidelines that outline the foundational knowledge and skills students should have at certain levels. The SIS activities — which are designed to supplement or guide, not replace, existing curricula — help develop these skills and knowledge. Not all educators use the same standards. For this reason, many of the activities address multiple standards and guidelines. ENGLISH LANGUAGE ARTS Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects These standards, published in 2010, were created by a group of educators and experts in various subjects. In 2009, the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the Council of Chief State Schools Officers began developing the Common Core State Standards — sets of expected knowledge and skills that represent what K-12 students should know and be able to do in math and English language arts and literacy. The literacy standards can be integrated into any history and social studies curriculum. The Common Core State Standards are used by teachers across the nation. Forty-two states and the District of Columbia have adopted at least some of these standards.
